newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian bonds steady, unmoved by rating hopes.
newsitem.headline: Croatian bonds steady, unmoved by rating hopes.

text.p: Croatia's second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds traded flat at 8.45 percent above par on Wednesday, seemingly immune to positive rating signals that moved most stocks up.
Volume traded was 1,000 units and turnover totalled 3.86 million kuna. The three-year bonds yield an annual 8.0 percent.
The country expects to get its first sovereign rating from three leading international agencies any time soon. The assessment is widely hoped to be a solid BB+ or equivalent, if not higher.
Meanwhile the local market was confused by conflicting reports on the maiden issue of kuna-denominated Eurobonds, officially listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange this week.
The bourse said "free and unrestricted secondary trade" could only begin on February 17.
The bonds were quoted indicatively at 98.5/105 by Zagrebacka Banka and 99.9/100.9 by Trgovacka Banka, two of four banks that agreed to make a market in them in Croatia.
The two-year Eurokuna bonds carry a fixed interest of 12.5 percent a year and have a semi-annual coupon. They mature on December 18, 1998. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
